skills.name: Virtual Hub Routing Concepts Reference
skills.description: Foundational reference guide covering hub route tables, routing intents, policies, connections, association, propagation, labels, and static route configuration for virtual hub routing design and troubleshooting.
skills.skill_body:
Use this reference to understand core virtual hub routing concepts. A virtual hub router manages all routing between gateways using BGP and can contain multiple gateway types (Site-to-site VPN, ExpressRoute, Point-to-site, Azure Firewall). The router provides transit connectivity between virtual networks and supports up to 50 Gbps aggregate throughput. Key concepts include: route tables (organize and filter routes), routing intents and policies (define traffic forwarding rules), connections (link gateways and virtual networks), association (connect routes to connections), propagation (distribute routes across the hub), and labels (tag routes for policy application). Static routes can be configured in virtual network connections for custom routing behavior.

## Objective

Provide foundational routing concepts and terminology for virtual hub design
## Applicable Signals

- Designing virtual hub routing topology
- Troubleshooting routing behavior
- Onboarding team members to Virtual WAN routing model
- Planning multi-gateway connectivity

## Contraindications

- Immediate operational troubleshooting requiring step-by-step remediation
- Configuration of specific gateway types
- Real-time incident response

## Constraints

- Applies to Standard Virtual WAN customers only
- Maximum aggregate throughput is 50 Gbps per virtual hub

## Output Contract

- Clear understanding of routing concepts (route tables, intents, policies, association, propagation, labels) enabling informed routing design decisions and topology planning
